=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:3496-3498 (same block in .github/workflows/clarify.yml:2339-2341; helper path scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:7160-7165, 3388-3398) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When the check-run annotations fetch fails (`|| rm -f "${FP_ANNOTATIONS_FILE}" || true`), or when `FP_JOB_ID` is not numeric, the workflow still calls the helper. The helper (`_cmd_phase_failure_fingerprint`) treats the missing file as `annotations = []` and emits a valid `AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_V1` marker with reason "ok" and the `no-error-line` fallback.
  WHY: During an annotations API outage, different failures on the same step collapse into one phase+step fingerprint, so `evaluate_failure_fingerprint_breaker` (orchestrate_lib.py:3847-3868) can trip at `STALL_FINGERPRINT_REPEAT_MAX` (default 2) and apply `ai:plan-failed`/`ai:clarify-failed` to non-identical failures. This contradicts the documented fail-open contract in README.md:3598, the agents.d and changelog.d fragments, and plan.yml:3472-3473. All five reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3310-3333 (`_phase_failure_failed_step`; workflow jq selector `[.jobs[]? | select(.runner_name == env.RUNNER_NAME) | .id][0]`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The job lookup takes the first job whose runner name matches, without filtering for the failed job or the current attempt's active job.
  WHY: If a runner name is reused across jobs in the same run, a previously completed job can be picked, which gives an empty or wrong step name and a generic or wrong fingerprint, so the stall breaker misses real repeats. Source severity was MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected this as matching the documented assemble_failure_evidence selection and listed it only as hardening; z-ai_glm-5_3-flash dropped it as unverifiable against the cited lines.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3362-3375 (`_phase_failure_failed_step`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When the first failure step's `name` is not a string (e.g. `None` for an unnamed step), the failed-step selection returns an empty string, so `phase_failure_fingerprint` treats it as `step_unknown` and emits no marker.
  WHY: An unnamed failed `run:` step never gets a fingerprint marker, so the breaker never sees the repeat and the stall loop can continue indefinitely; the reviewer suggests falling back to a stable identifier such as the step number. Source severity was MAJOR. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 called this the intended fail-open path.
- README.md:3598 (also agents.d/stuck-states-p3a-fingerprint-markers.md:2, changelog.d/stuck-states-p3a-fingerprint-markers.md:2) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The documentation promises that an API error means no marker is posted.
  WHY: Annotations-fetch API errors do not skip marker emission, which can confuse operators and lead to logic errors in the breaker. Source severity was NIT.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:~10130-10180 (`_pff_run_step`) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The smoke test stages only `workflow_failure_heal.py` and not `gh_helpers.sh`, so `gh_retry` may be undefined. The jobs call would then fail with `FP_REASON="jobs_unavailable"` and the "ok" assertion `body.endswith("\n\n" + marker)` would fail.
  WHY: This affects only the test harness. Source severity was NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rejected it because of the fallback shim at plan.yml:3454 / clarify.yml:2297 (`type gh_retry >/dev/null 2>&1 || gh_retry() { "$@"; }`).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml (and the same code in .github/workflows/clarify.yml, plus scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py):plan.yml:3496 and clarify.yml:2339 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A failed annotations lookup, or a `FP_JOB_ID` that does not match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, still posts a valid `AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_V1` marker built only from phase + step + "no-error-line", and the log says `outcome=emitted`. This contradicts the README P3a bullet, the changelog fragment and the agents fragment.
  WHY: During an annotations outage, distinct failures of the same step share one fp, so `evaluate_failure_fingerprint_breaker` (orchestrate_lib.py:3847-3868) trips at `STALL_FINGERPRINT_REPEAT_MAX` (default 2) and applies `ai:plan-failed`/`ai:clarify-failed`. Suggested fix: set `FP_REASON="annotations_unavailable"` and skip the helper (about 3 lines per workflow), or correct the docs.
- HARDENING: .github/workflows/plan.yml:3494 and .github/workflows/clarify.yml:2337 (jq selector), plus scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `_phase_failure_failed_step`
  PROBLEM: Both take the first job whose runner_name matches, whatever its status, so a completed job on a reused runner name could give the wrong step and annotations.
  WHY: Suggested fix: prefer `status == "in_progress"` and fall back to the first match (4 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE. All deliverables are present. The failing copilot-pull-request-reviewer check is an infrastructure error (custom_instructions_too_large) unrelated to the diff.

Rejected gemini's `_phase_failure_failed_step` finding (it matches the documented selection, and a non-string name gives step_unknown, which is fail-open), gemini's "tests fail per check-runs" TASK_GAP, and minimax's "gh_retry undefined" finding (fallback at plan.yml:3454 / clarify.yml:2297). (4 related items)
